title: Error types
game_role: The code you fixed prints the player's status at the start of the game.
objective: Recognize Python's error types, read error messages and fix errors
story: The last room of the workshop is a detective's office! The desk is covered with broken code, and all of it shows red error messages. But error messages aren't our enemies, they're clues: they tell us what broke and where. Today we become error detectives.

sections.title: How to read an error message
sections.body:
An error message holds three important pieces of information:

- **Line number:** where is the problem?
- **Error type:** like `NameError` or `TypeError`
- **Description:** the short sentence next to the type

Go to the line first, then look at the error type. Most of the time the problem is on that line or the one just above it.

sections.title: The most common errors
sections.body:
- `SyntaxError`: a writing rule is broken (a forgotten `:` or parenthesis)
- `IndentationError`: wrong indentation
- `NameError`: a name that isn't defined (usually a typo)
- `TypeError`: the wrong types used together (`"Age: " + 12`)
- `ValueError`: the type is right but the value isn't suitable (`int("twelve")`)
- `IndexError`: a position that isn't in the list (`items[10]`)
- `KeyError`: a key that isn't in the dictionary
- `ZeroDivisionError`: dividing by zero
- `AttributeError`: a method that type doesn't have (`5.upper()`)
- `ModuleNotFoundError`: a module that doesn't exist

sections.title: Checking types
sections.body:
Many errors come from mixed-up types. Use `type()` to look at a value's type:

```python
age = "12"
print(type(age))       # <class 'str'>
print(int(age) + 1)    # 13
```

When joining text and numbers, use `str()` or an f-string: `f"Age: {age}"`

sections.title: Detective tactics
sections.body:
- Put `print()` in between to see what's inside your variables
- Run the code in small pieces
- Read the error message out loud; it really says a lot
- Could the list be empty? Could the number be zero? Think about edge cases

In a few days, on Discovery Island, we'll learn to catch these errors without the program crashing (`try` and `except`).

examples.title: Fix the type mix-up
examples.code:
age = 12
print("I am " + str(age))
print(f"I am {age}")
text = "7"
print(int(text) + 3)

examples.title: Look at the type
Looking safely
examples.code:
items = ["sword", "shield"]
hero = {"name": "Piko"}
print(items[-1])
print(hero.get("gold", 0))
nums = []
print(sum(nums) / len(nums) if nums else 0)
examples.note: Each of these lines shows a way to prevent an error.

tasks.title: Fix the TypeError
tasks.prompt: This code raises a `TypeError`. Fix it so that it prints `I am 12`.
hints: Text and a number can't be joined with +.
Turn age into text with str(age), or use an f-string.

tasks.title: Fix the IndexError
tasks.prompt: This code wants to print the last item in the bag but fails. Fix it. It should still print the last item even if the bag grows.
hints: Positions start at 0; the last index of a 3-item list is 2.
The shortcut that always gives the last item: items[-1]

tasks.title: Fix the KeyError
tasks.prompt: There's no `gold` key in the dictionary, so the code fails. Fix it with `get()`: if the key is missing, it should print `0`.
hints: hero.get("gold", 0) gives 0 if the key is missing.

challenge.title: Dividing by zero
challenge.prompt: `average(nums)` returns the average, but with an empty list it raises a `ZeroDivisionError`. Fix it so it returns `0` when the list is empty.
hints: Check whether the list is empty before dividing.

project_task.title: Bug hunt
project_task.prompt:
Three bugs have sneaked into Piko's game! Run the code, read the error messages and fix them one by one. When it works it should print:

```
Player: Piko
Health: 100
First item: sword
```
project_task.starter:
player = {"name": "Piko", "hp": 100}
items = ["sword", "potion"]

project_task.solution:
player = {"name": "Piko", "hp": 100}
items = ["sword", "potion"]

print("Player: " + player["name"])
print("Health: " + str(player["hp"]))
print("First item: " + items[0])
hints: The first bug is a NameError: look closely at the variable's name.
The second bug is a TypeError: turn the number into text with str().
The third is a wrong result: the first item is items[0]
